title: "Personal breadth" proxy -- non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #170 (backend-watchlist-breadth-proxy), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: bullish_pct/bearish_pct/neutral_pct (GET /api/watchlist/breadth) are each independently rounded to 1 decimal place, so they don't always sum to exactly 100.0 -- e.g. an even 1/3-1/3-1/3 computable split yields 33.3 + 33.3 + 33.3 = 99.9, confirmed by this PR's own test_mixed_watchlist_and_portfolio_with_an_unavailable_ticker test. Not a bug (each percentage is independently correct), but worth a doc note (docs/Analyse.md / docs/architecture/API.md) that the three percentages aren't guaranteed to sum to 100.0, or a tweak to derive the last bucket's percentage as the remainder -- so the frontend-breadth-widget task doesn't display something that looks like a rounding bug to an end user.

docs/Analyse.md's new "Personal breadth proxy" subsection is nested under "## 7. Portfolio-Level Rules (risk management overlay)", alongside the 2%/6% rules, stop-loss placement, trade grading, and existing-position exit signals -- but it isn't itself a risk-management/position-sizing rule, it's an informational context aggregate (closer in kind to Screen 1/Tide, section 2). Arguable, not clear-cut -- worth reconsidering whether it deserves its own top-level section instead, but reasonable people could keep it where it is given it also spans the portfolio.

backend/app/api/routers/watchlist.py's new _tide_trend (line ~71) duplicates _compute_signal's fetch-and-catch logic (identical try/except DataProviderError around get_daily_ohlcv/get_weekly_ohlcv, then analyse()) instead of reusing it -- could instead be `result = _compute_signal(ticker, provider); return result.screens['tide']['trend'] if result else None`. Not a bug, but if the two functions' shared error-handling contract ever changes, a maintainer could update one and miss the other, silently reintroducing the exact code-path divergence this module's own docstring says it's trying to avoid. Flagged by code-review (PR #170).

get_watchlist_breadth's docstring/decision record claims 'No new provider calls result either way, since every tracked ticker's OHLCV is already being fetched for this same request's own per-ticker signal computation' -- but GET /api/watchlist/breadth is its own separate HTTP request, not one that also computes GET /api/watchlist's or GET /api/portfolio's per-ticker signals in the same call. Whether _tide_trend's fetches actually hit CachedDataProvider's cache depends on whether one of those other endpoints was hit recently and the cache TTL hasn't expired -- if the breadth widget is the first thing loaded in a session, this endpoint does a full, uncached 2N-fetch + N-full-analyse() pass. Worth correcting the docstring's wording to describe this as 'reuses the shared OHLCV cache when warm' rather than implying no fetch ever happens, and/or considering the latency-at-scale question (sequential per-ticker fetch/analyse over a large watchlist+portfolio) if this ever becomes noticeably slow in practice. Flagged by code-review (PR #170).
